function.name: list_node_types
function.description: The live catalog of every node type — its category, settings (key, type, required, default), outputs and outputSchema. Always read this first; it is the only reliable source for valid `nodes[*].type` values and their `data` keys. (GET /api/automation/workflow-nodes)

function.name: lookup_sales_channels
function.description: Sales channels as {id, name}. Feeds any node setting of type `multiselect` whose apiEndpoint is /automation/lookups/sales-channels — the values stored are the numeric ids, never the channel names. (GET /api/automation/lookups/sales-channels)

function.name: lookup_warehouses
function.description: Warehouses as {id, name}, for warehouse-valued node settings. (GET /api/automation/lookups/warehouses)

function.name: lookup_tags
function.description: Order tags, for the Apply Tags node's `tags` setting. (GET /api/automation/lookups/tags)

function.name: list_workflows
function.description: Paginated list of workflows with run stats. Use it to avoid creating a duplicate, and to find an existing workflow to update. (GET /api/automation/workflows)

function.name: validate_workflow
function.description: Check a graph without saving. Verifies exactly one trigger node, that every edge references existing nodes, and that every non-trigger node has an incoming connection. Call this before create and before update — it is free and catches the structural mistakes. (POST /api/automation/workflows/validate)

nodes.description: The node list, same shape as on create.

edges.description: The edge list, same shape as on create.

function.name: create_workflow
function.description: Create a workflow in Draft status from a node/edge graph. The trigger type is derived from the trigger node — you do not set it. Drafts never fire. (POST /api/automation/workflows)

name.example: TikTok Shop: email on new order

description.description: What it does and why it exists. Worth writing — it is what the next person reads before deciding whether to disable it.

category.description: Free-text grouping, max 50 chars (e.g. orders, imports, inventory).

nodes.description: One object per node: `id` (string, max 64, unique in the graph), `type` (a `type` from the node catalog), `position` {x, y} (numeric — the canvas coordinates the builder will draw it at), `data` (object — the node's settings, keyed by the `settings[*].key` the catalog lists; required even when empty), optional `label`.

edges.description: One object per connection: `id`, `source` (node id), `target` (node id); optional `sourceHandle` (required to leave a branching node — `true`/`false` on IF, `case0…`/`fallback` on Switch), `targetHandle`, `label`, `branchLabel`.

viewport.description: Canvas position {x, y, zoom} the builder opens at. Defaults are fine.

preview_mode.description: When true, every run executes triggers, conditions and lookups for real but SKIPS every state-changing Action/Integration step (emails, Slack, webhooks, order and inventory writes), recording what each would have done. Default false.

function.name: get_workflow
function.description: One workflow with its full graph, derived triggerType/triggerConfig, and publish state. (GET /api/automation/workflows/{workflow})

function.name: update_workflow
function.description: Update name, description, category, graph, settings or preview_mode. All fields optional. Submitting `nodes` re-derives the trigger type and trigger config, so send the WHOLE graph — a partial node list silently drops the nodes you left out. (PUT /api/automation/workflows/{workflow})

nodes.description: The complete node list. Omit the key entirely to leave the graph untouched.

preview_mode.description: Toggle preview (dry-run) mode on an existing workflow.

function.name: publish_workflow
function.description: Validate then publish, making the trigger live. On validation failure nothing changes and the errors come back as 422. On success the version increments and publishedAt is set. A workflow only ever fires once published. (POST /api/automation/workflows/{workflow}/publish)

function.name: toggle_workflow
function.description: Flip between published (live) and disabled (paused). Only those two states can be toggled — a draft must be published first. This is the off switch; prefer it to delete. (POST /api/automation/workflows/{workflow}/toggle)

function.name: execute_workflow
function.description: Run a published workflow by hand against a payload you supply, instead of waiting for a real trigger. Queued asynchronously — the response is the execution record at status `pending`; poll get-execution for the result. (POST /api/automation/workflows/{workflow}/execute)

trigger_payload.description: The data the trigger node would have emitted, shaped like that trigger's `outputSchema`. Omit it and event triggers fall back to sample data built from the most recent matching record.

function.name: list_executions
function.description: Run history for one workflow — status, duration, trigger reference, error. (GET /api/automation/workflows/{workflow}/executions)

function.name: get_execution
function.description: One execution with its per-step results — each step's status, logs, and (in preview mode) the input the skipped step would have used. This is where you read what actually happened. (GET /api/automation/workflow-executions/{execution})

function.name: clone_workflow
function.description: Duplicate a workflow as a new Draft named "<name> (Copy)". Use it to change a live workflow safely — clone, edit the clone, test it, then swap. (POST /api/automation/workflows/{workflow}/clone)

function.name: delete_workflow
function.description: Permanently delete a workflow. Irreversible, and it takes the run history with it — disable instead unless the user explicitly asked to delete. (DELETE /api/automation/workflows/{workflow})
